business_summary: Microsoft sells software, cloud computing and devices to businesses, governments and consumers. FY2026 (ended 2026-06-30) revenue was $331.839B, up 18% from $281.724B, across three reported segments: Productivity & Business Processes (Microsoft 365, Teams, LinkedIn, Dynamics) $139.996B; Intelligent Cloud (Azure, server products, GitHub) $137.791B; More Personal Computing (Windows, Xbox, Surface, search advertising) $54.052B. Azure passed $100B of annual revenue for the first time in FY2026 and grew 43% in Q4. Most revenue is recurring subscription or consumption-based, and commercial remaining performance obligation (contracted future revenue) reached $678B, up 84%. From FY2027 Microsoft reports in two new segments, 'Agents and Infra' ($268.1B FY2026 revenue recast) and 'Devices and Consumer' ($63.7B). The business should still be winning in 5-10 years because enterprises run their operations on Microsoft software, switching costs are very high, and Microsoft is one of a handful of credible platforms for the AI buildout. The open question this year is not demand but capital intensity: cash capex nearly doubled to $115.948B in FY2026 (plus $24.608B of finance-lease right-of-use assets), so free cash flow FELL to $66.987B from $71.611B even as revenue grew 18%. For FY2027 management guided to double-digit revenue and operating-income growth, operating margin down less than 1 point, Q1 capex (incl. finance leases) above $50B, and continued positive free cash flow.

moat.type: High switching costs (Microsoft 365, Windows, Azure, Dynamics), network effects (Teams, LinkedIn, GitHub), scale economies in cloud infrastructure, deep enterprise distribution and contracted backlog

quality.roic: ~31% estimated: NOPAT $125.1B (operating income $155.237B x (1 - 19.4% effective tax rate)) on average invested capital ~$405.3B (equity + total debt + finance-lease liabilities - cash and short-term investments, FY2025/FY2026 average). Derived from 10-K figures, not a reported metric.
quality.net_debt_to_ebitda: ~0.15x. Net cash of $36.5B excluding leases ($76.843B cash + short-term investments vs $40.294B total debt); including $66.594B of finance-lease liabilities, net debt is ~$30.0B against EBITDA of ~$199.6B (operating income $155.237B + depreciation $34.3B + intangible amortization $4.7B + finance-lease ROU amortization $5.403B). Finance-lease liabilities have grown from $27.145B (FY2024) to $66.594B (FY2026) and are the fastest-growing obligation on the balance sheet.
quality.fcf_positive: yes, but shrinking: FY2026 FCF $66.987B (operating cash flow $182.935B - capex $115.948B), down from $71.611B in FY2025. Net of $3.101B finance-lease principal payments, $63.886B.

valuation.method: Blend (simple average) of two methods run through code/valuation.py on 2026-10-28. INPUTS UNCHANGED from the 2026-09-17 refresh, by design: no new financial filing has been published since then (Q1 FY2027 results are released after the close TODAY, 2026-10-28), and the fed funds range is still 3.75-4.00% (the September hike was already priced into our multiples). Per the playbook rule, we do not move fair value without a named changed fundamental, so the band is identical; only the price changed. (1) P/E: 26x / 30x / 34x on FY2026 non-GAAP diluted EPS of $17.28 -> $449.28 / $518.40 / $587.52. 30x is roughly where a wide-moat ~18% grower with 47% operating margins has historically traded; 26x reflects a de-rating if AI capex disappoints, 34x continued AI-driven acceleration. (2) FCF yield: 3.8% / 3.2% / 2.7% on FY2026 FCF per share of $8.99 ($66.987B / 7,453M diluted shares) -> $236.58 / $280.94 / $332.96. Blended band $342.93 / $399.67 / $460.24. Margin of safety at $528.38 = -32.2% (NEGATIVE; worse than -24.5% at the last refresh purely because the price rose ~6%). SENSITIVITY, stated honestly: the two methods disagree sharply. On earnings alone MSFT trades at 29.4x trailing GAAP EPS ($17.95) and 30.6x non-GAAP ($17.28) - right at our P/E base of $518, i.e. roughly FAIR, not cheap. On cash, the FCF yield at $528.38 is just 1.70% versus a 3.75-4.00% fed funds rate. The blend is dragged down by the FCF method because cash capex ($115.9B) plus finance leases ($24.6B) is ~4x depreciation ($34.3B). A further caveat for FY2027 onward: management extended datacentre/office building useful lives from 15 to 25 years from the start of FY2027 and is shifting future leases from finance to operating; both make future reported earnings and reported capex look better without any change in cash economics, so P/E on FY2027 EPS should be read with that in mind.

bull_case: Wide moat intact and arguably widening: commercial remaining performance obligation (contracted future revenue not yet recognised) jumped 84% to $678B in Q4 FY2026, the clearest evidence yet that customers are committing years of spend in advance.
Azure passed $100B of annual revenue in FY2026 and still grew 43% in Q4, with management guiding 44-45% constant-currency growth for Q1 FY2027 - acceleration, not deceleration, at enormous scale.
Exceptional economics: 67.9% gross margin, 46.8% operating margin, ~31% estimated ROIC, and net cash of $36.5B excluding leases. FY2026 net income $133.749B on $331.839B of revenue.
AI is monetising, not just costing: Microsoft 365 Copilot surpassed 30 million paid seats, giving Microsoft a per-seat upsell on an installed base it already owns.
Diversified and durable: Productivity ($140.0B) and Intelligent Cloud ($137.8B) are now similarly sized, so no single product carries the company; FY2026 diluted EPS grew 32% GAAP / 22% non-GAAP.
risks: VALUATION IS THE PRIMARY RISK, AND WE ARE HONEST ABOUT IT: at $528.38 (Alpaca, 2026-10-28) MSFT trades ~32% above our base fair value of $399.67 and ~15% above the $460.24 high end of our band. On our framework this stock is OVERVALUED and is not a buy at this price. The free-cash-flow yield at today's price is just 1.70% versus a 3.75-4.00% fed funds rate. Even on earnings alone (30.6x non-GAAP) it is at fair, not below it. Sell-side consensus (MarketBeat, Aug 2026: $560.98 average target) is above the price, but analyst targets are not our valuation and we do not anchor on them.

Free cash flow is going backwards: FY2026 FCF of $66.987B was BELOW FY2025's $71.611B despite 18% revenue growth, because cash capex nearly doubled from $64.551B to $115.948B. Q1 FY2027 capex alone is guided to over $50B. If this continues, FCF could fall again in FY2027.

The AI capex bet is unproven and enormous. Capex ($115.9B) is now 3.4x depreciation ($34.3B), which means today's earnings are flattered relative to the depreciation charge that this asset base will eventually carry. If AI demand disappoints, both margins and returns on capital fall hard.

Off-balance-sheet-ish leverage is building: finance-lease liabilities rose from $27.145B (FY2024) to $46.172B (FY2025) to $66.594B (FY2026). This is real debt-like obligation used to fund datacentres and it does not show up in the headline 'net cash' figure.

Accounting tailwinds flatter FY2027 reported numbers: from the start of FY2027 Microsoft extended the useful life of datacentres and office buildings from 15 to 25 years (CFO: 'a minimal benefit' to FY2027 operating income) and expects more future datacentre leases to be operating rather than finance leases, which removes them from reported capex. Calendar-2026 capex expectation moved from ~$190B to ~$175B mainly because of this accounting change, not lower spending. Lower reported capex and depreciation will make FCF and margins look better than the underlying cash economics; we will track operating-lease commitments alongside finance leases. (Sourced from earnings-call coverage, not yet verified in a filing.)

Physical constraints on the buildout: on 2026-10-16 Microsoft was reported (Bloomberg, citing The Telegraph) to have pulled out of anchoring Nscale's planned UK datacentre in Loughton, Essex, reportedly because grid power may not arrive until the 2030s. Power and site availability, not demand, may cap Azure growth.

Earnings quality: FY2026 GAAP net income ($133.749B) was boosted by discrete items including a $3.2B gain on the Anthropic investment. Non-GAAP net income was $128.786B. Mark-to-market gains on AI-company stakes are not repeatable operating profit.

Macro and rates: the Fed raised its target range by 25bp in September 2026 to 3.75-4.00%, core inflation remains above target, and economists/markets surveyed in late October largely expect a further hike in December. Higher risk-free rates compress the multiple investors will pay for long-duration growth, and a corporate IT spending slowdown would hit cloud consumption and seat growth.
Regulatory/antitrust scrutiny in the US and EU over cloud bundling, the OpenAI relationship, and AI market power.
Segment reporting changes from FY2027 ('Agents and Infra' / 'Devices and Consumer') reduce comparability and make it harder to track Azure and Windows separately over time.
what_would_break_thesis: Azure constant-currency revenue growth falls below 20% for two consecutive quarters (guidance for Q1 FY2027 is 44-45%; a fall to sub-20% would mean the AI cloud thesis has broken).
Total company revenue declines year over year for two consecutive quarters.
Company-wide gross margin falls below 60% for two consecutive quarters (FY2026: 67.9%).
Operating margin falls below 38% for two consecutive quarters (FY2026: 46.8%) - the signal that AI capex depreciation is overwhelming the P&L.

FY2027 full-year operating margin falls more than 3 percentage points below FY2026's 46.8% (i.e. below ~43.8%). Management guided a decline of less than 1 point, and that guide already includes the useful-life extension tailwind, so a miss of this size would mean AI costs are running well ahead of AI revenue.
Free cash flow declines year over year for a third consecutive fiscal year, or turns negative for any full fiscal year (FY2025 $71.6B -> FY2026 $67.0B is already one year of decline).
Net-debt-to-EBITDA including finance-lease liabilities rises above 1.5x (currently ~0.15x), or finance-lease liabilities exceed $150B.
Estimated ROIC falls below 15% on a sustained multi-year basis (currently ~31%).
Commercial remaining performance obligation declines year over year.

A serious accounting restatement, an SEC enforcement action, or a material governance red flag - in particular any restatement of datacentre asset useful lives (beyond the disclosed FY2027 15->25 year building extension), any further useful-life extension for servers/network equipment that is not supported by operating history, or a restatement of revenue recognised on AI-related related-party transactions.
catalysts: Q1 FY2027 earnings TODAY, 2026-10-28, after the market close (webcast 2:30pm PT): the test of whether Azure hits the guided ~45% constant-currency growth (aggregator previews cite consensus revenue ~$90.6B and non-GAAP EPS ~$4.71-4.72) and how big Q1 capex actually was (guided >$50B incl. finance leases). This thesis must be refreshed within days of that release; refresh_due is set to 2026-11-04.
Evidence of return on AI capex - specifically Intelligent Cloud / 'Agents and Infra' operating margin holding up while the depreciation from the FY2026-27 buildout starts to hit the P&L.

A price pullback toward the $460 high end, the $400 base, or the $343 low end of our band. The 250-day low from the Alpaca feed is $349.21 (high $551.08), so this is not an impossible price; earnings-day moves for MSFT have been large (e.g. ~+17% intraday on 2026-07-30).
Capex growth normalising back toward depreciation, which would cause reported free cash flow to jump sharply and resolve the earnings-versus-cash-flow disagreement in our valuation.
Copilot paid seats compounding well beyond 30 million, proving AI is a revenue line and not just a cost line.
